NEW DELHI: Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction's candidate for the Rejinagar Assembly bypoll, has decided to withdraw his candidature, dealing another setback to the faction a day after its Nandigram nominee also pulled out.Chowdhury said he was withdrawing because the faction's newly allotted election symbol would be difficult to make familiar to voters in the short time available before the October 6 bypoll.The decision means Mamata's faction has now lost its candidates in both Nandigram and Rejinagar, two of the seats going to the polls in West Bengal on October 6.Chowdhury's announcement came a day after Sanchita Pradhan Dey, the faction's candidate in Nandigram, withdrew her nomination. She had met West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari with her husband on Thursday, but did not publicly explain her decision to quit.After Dey's withdrawal, Mamata's faction backed Congress candidate Milan Pradhan in Nandigram. Pradhan was subsequently arrested by police in connection with pending cases dating back to 2007.The developments triggered allegations from opposition parties that state agencies were being used to influence the bypolls.Those allegations have not been independently established.The withdrawals follow the Election Commission's interim decision to stop both rival TMC factions from using the party's original name and its 'flowers and grass' symbol while it considers their competing claims.The EC allotted Mamata's faction the name 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress' and the 'football player' symbol. The rival faction led by Arup Roy was given the name 'Democratic Trinamool Congress' and the 'envelope' symbol.The poll panel said the temporary arrangement was necessary to ensure candidates from both factions could contest the bypolls. It said otherwise returning officers could have been required to reject their nomination papers because of the dispute over the party's identity and frozen symbol.Mamata has moved the Supreme Court against the EC's decision to prevent her faction from using the original TMC name and its traditional symbol.The EC has said both factions will be treated as recognised political parties in West Bengal, Meghalaya and Tripura for the time being. The new names and symbols will remain in place while the larger dispute over control of the party is decided.The October 6 bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar will therefore take place against the backdrop of the split, with Mamata's faction now having lost its original candidates in both constituencies.
Article Summary: Rabiul Alam Chowdhury, the Mamata Banerjee-led faction's candidate for the Rejinagar Assembly bypoll, has decided to withdraw his candidature. The decision means Mamata's faction has now lost its candidates in both Nandigram and Rejingar, two of the seats going to the polls on October 6.

Article Title: Maharashtra TET paper leak: Employees hid question papers in shoes, paid Rs 8,000 each
Article Text:

How the papers allegedly got out

Leak exposed a day before exam

NEW DELHI: The Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test paper allegedly walked out of an Agra printing press hidden inside shoe insoles, with two employees paid Rs 8,000 each to smuggle out the confidential examination material, according to a chargesheet filed by Thane City police.The chargesheet, filed before a Bhiwandi court on Friday, names 18 accused, including alleged mastermind Bijendra Gupta, and lays out how investigators traced the leak from the printing press to those allegedly trying to sell the papers in Maharashtra. Sixteen accused have been arrested, while two others, Ashok Sav and Prakash Misal, remain absconding, police said.According to the chargesheet, the leak was traced to Mahim Patran Pvt Ltd, an Agra-based printing press tasked with producing the confidential TET examination material.Between June 15 and 17, two employees and a former staffer allegedly concealed folded question papers inside their shoe insoles while leaving the premises. Security guards frisked their clothes but allegedly did not check their footwear, allowing the papers to be taken outside, the chargesheet said.The state had prepared four separate sets of question papers for the two TET papers to maintain confidentiality and allow one set to be selected on examination day.Investigators allege that all four sets were nevertheless taken out of the press.The employees were allegedly paid Rs 8,000 each and promised land plots in Agra in return for stealing the papers, according to the chargesheet.The racket came to light on June 27, a day before the TET was scheduled to be held. Deputy commissioner of Police Pavan Bansod received information that three men were allegedly trying to sell question papers to a Bhiwandi resident.Police then laid a trap using decoy personnel in Kongaon and detained the suspects, recovering four sets of question papers. Officials of the Maharashtra state council of examination later verified that the seized material matched the actual TET paper.The examination, scheduled for June 28, was subsequently postponed.Police have booked the accused under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita relating to cheating, criminal breach of trust and criminal conspiracy, along with Maharashtra laws dealing with examination malpractice. A special investigation team is probing the case.Investigators have identified Gupta, a former coaching-class teacher, as the alleged mastermind. Police said he had previously been implicated in another examination paper leak in Odisha.The chargesheet cites money trails, technical evidence and the recovery of an original question paper from the Bihar residence of a relative of Gupta as evidence in the alleged supply chain. Police said a supplementary chargesheet would be filed as the investigation continues.
Article Summary: The Maharashtra Teacher Eligibility Test paper allegedly walked out of an Agra printing press hidden inside shoe insoles. Two employees were allegedly paid Rs 8,000 each and promised land plots in Agra in return for stealing the papers. Sixteen accused have been arrested, while two others, Ashok Sav and Prakash Misal, remain absconding.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday inaugurated a two-day international conference on “The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics”, organised by the National Green Tribunal (NGT) at Vigyan Bhawan in New Delhi.The conference, being held on September 19 and 20, brings together judges, environmental experts, senior government officials and representatives of various environmental and judicial institutions from India and abroad. Judicial representatives from 17 countries are also participating in the event.Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant, Union Environment, Forest and Climate Change Minister Bhupender Yadav, Attorney General R Venkataramani and NGT Chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava attended the inaugural session.The conference will feature four technical sessions focusing on key environmental and climate-related issues. According to the NGT, the discussions will examine major challenges facing the world, identify gaps in policy-making and implementation, and explore ways to strengthen institutional cooperation.The event also aims to facilitate the exchange of successful environmental practices and strengthen environmental justice amid growing challenges linked to climate change, development and governance.President Droupadi Murmu will attend the valedictory session on Sunday. Union minister Manohar Lal, Supreme Court judge Justice PS Narasimha, NGT Chairperson Justice Prakash Shrivastava and Solicitor General Tushar Mehta are also scheduled to attend the concluding session.The conference is expected to work towards developing a roadmap for addressing present and future environmental and climate challenges.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday inaugurated a two-day international conference on ‘The Future of Environment and Climate Dynamics’ The conference, being held on September 19 and 20, brings together judges, environmental experts, senior government officials and representatives of various environmental and judicial institutions from India and abroad.

Article Title: 'Delhi a terrifying daily story for women': Rahul, Priyanka slam Amit Shah over teen's gangrape-murder

NEW DELHI: Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have spoken out over the alleged gang rape and murder of a teenage girl in Delhi, with both questioning the authorities over women's safety and demanding accountability for the incident.Rahul Gandhi, leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, criticised the Delhi Police and questioned the responsibility of Union home minister Amit Shah, under whose ministry the force functions. He said the teenager was gang-raped and murdered before her body was dumped in an open field, and questioned how the police remained unaware of the crime for days.In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi described the incident as a "horrific act of brutality" in the national capital. He also dismissed the idea that Delhi was providing women with a safe environment, saying the city had instead become a source of fear for women."It's unfortunate that Delhi is no longer the capital today; it has become a terrifying daily story for women," he said.Rahul directly questioned Shah over the responsibility for women's safety in Delhi. He pointed out that the Delhi Police is under the Union home ministry and asked who should ultimately be held responsible for the safety of women in the capital."Amit Shah ji, Delhi Police is under your control. Ultimately, whose responsibility is women's safety?" he said.He also criticised the functioning of the Delhi Police, asking whether its role had been reduced to intimidating ordinary citizens while criminals continued to operate without fear."Or has the job of Delhi Police been reduced to just intimidating and threatening ordinary citizens? Because the criminals are roaming around fearlessly," Gandhi said.Calling for immediate action, the Congress leader demanded that those responsible for the crime be arrested and punished strictly. He also sought accountability for what he described as criminal negligence."The beasts must be arrested immediately, strict action and punishment must be taken, and accountability for this criminal negligence must be fixed," he said.Rahul Gandhi ended his post by linking women's safety to India's wider progress, saying, "India cannot move forward without women's safety."Priyanka Gandhi also raised concerns over the case, saying the crime against the teenager represented an extreme form of brutality. She noted that another minor girl had allegedly been raped just days earlier and questioned whether authorities were taking sufficient responsibility for women's safety."In Delhi, all limits of cruelty were crossed against a 17-year-old girl, and after that, she was brutally murdered. Just a few days earlier, another minor girl was raped," she said in a post on X.Priyanka Gandhi further questioned the government's response to crimes against women. She argued that while there was discussion about women's development, women continued to face violence without what she described as concrete action against perpetrators."No one in the country is willing to take responsibility for women's safety—only empty talk about women's development is offered," she said.She claimed that hundreds of women face atrocities and violence and alleged that victims can struggle to get action from authorities, including the registration of FIRs."Hundreds of women face atrocities and violence, but they cannot hope for concrete action against the perpetrators—FIRs aren't even filed," she said.Priyanka Gandhi also said the issue went beyond the individual case and reflected a wider failure to ensure women's basic rights. She argued that both society and the government had failed to provide women with adequate safety, freedom and equality."Both society and the government have completely failed in granting women their rights to safety, freedom, and equality," she said.A teenage girl was allegedly gang-raped and murdered in Delhi. Her body was subsequently dumped in an open field, with the police facing questions over the delay in detecting the crime.The case has triggered political criticism over women's safety in the capital, with Rahul Gandhi focusing on the Delhi Police's role and its accountability to the Union home ministry.Priyanka Gandhi also referred to another case involving a minor girl that was reported days before the teenager's rape and murder. She used the two incidents to question the wider response to crimes against women.
Article Summary: A teenage girl was allegedly gang-raped and murdered in Delhi. Her body was subsequently dumped in an open field. The case has triggered political criticism over women's safety in the capital. Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra have spoken out over the alleged gang rape and murder of a teenage girl.

Article Title: US national gets default bail in terror case
Article Text:
Rouse Avenue Court in Delhi has granted default bail to US national Matthew Aaron VanDyke

NEW DELHI: A special NIA court in Delhi Friday granted default bail to the US national arrested in March on terror charges for allegedly helping ethnic armed groups in India and Myanmar, days after the "incomplete" chargesheet filed by the investigating agency dropped charges under UAPA, reports Koushiki Saha.While granting bail to Matthew Aaron VanDyke, who has spent 180 days in custody, the court noted NIA's failure to complete its probe. Article Title: Extremely speedy action by probe agency can create doubt: SC
Article Text:
The Supreme Court acquitted the RPF official, saying the CBI failed to prove that the intermediary accepted the bribe on his behalf.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: The speed at which CBI sprang into action on a bribery complaint and laid a trap within hours to catch a public servant could give rise to suspicion, which, Supreme Court said, could not be brushed aside and had to be examined.Finding fault with CBI's investigation, Justices Dipankar Datta and N K Singh acquitted the official in a two-decade-old case as he was not caught with the bribe money. It was an intermediary who accepted it and CBI failed to prove it was meant for the accused, SC said.The complaint made in 2005 alleged that the accused, working as a divisional security commissioner in Railway Protection Force , had demanded illegal gratification from subordinate officials for transfers and postings. CBI immediately lodged an FIR and laid a trap just hours later, catching the intermediary.The intermediary, who alleged that he accepted the bribe on behalf of the official, was given a pardon.SC said since the FIR was lodged on Aug 4, 2005, at 2pm and CBI decided to lay the trap on the same day, the agency must have verified the authenticity of the complaint before the trap was planned. "It is surprising that CBI started the investigation of a cognisable offence by way of verifying the complaint of bribery even before the formal FIR was lodged...The entire trap was arranged between 2 pm to 4.30pm. While the investigating agency cannot be faulted for organising the trap in such an extraordinarily speedy manner, it can raise certain doubts. The trial court, however, brushed aside the doubts raised by the appellant," the bench said.The court said criminality under Prevention of Corruption Act did not arise merely because money changed hands. "Before criminal liability can be fastened upon the public servant, the prosecution must establish by reliable evidence that the intermediary was acting under the authority, direction or for the benefit of the accused and that the demand itself was attributable to the accused. Mere receipt of money by a third person cannot automatically result in criminal liability being imputed to a public servant," it said.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court acquitted the RPF official, saying the CBI failed to prove that the intermediary accepted the bribe on his behalf. Justices Dipankar Datta and N K Singh acquitted the official in a two-decade-old case as he was not caught with the bribe money.

What happened in Nithari

NEW DELHI: Surinder Koli, who was acquitted in the last remaining case linked to the 2006 Nithari serial killings, died by suicide at a tea stall in Haridwar on Friday, police said.His body was found at a tea stall in the Bhupatwala area, near the Lal Mata temple, where he had been living and working in recent months. Police said no suicide note had been found and an investigation was under way."Police received information this morning that a person had allegedly hanged himself. Our forensic team reached the spot. At present, it appears to be a case of suicide. The body is in police custody, and the panchanama and post-mortem proceedings are underway," police told PTI videos.Koli's death comes less than a year after the Supreme Court acquitted him in the final case connected to the Nithari killings and ordered his immediate release in November 2025. He had spent nearly two decades in prison after being arrested in connection with the disappearance and killings of children and young women in Noida.Koli, who was 30 when arrested in 2006, had worked as a domestic help at the Noida home of businessman Moninder Singh Pandher . He was convicted in multiple cases and awarded several death sentences before the convictions were overturned in subsequent appeals.The Supreme Court's final acquittal brought an end to the criminal cases against him related to Nithari.The Nithari killings came to light in December 2006 after human skeletal remains were found in a drain near bungalow D-5 in Sector 31, Noida, which belonged to Pandher. The discovery followed months of complaints over missing children and young women from the area.s in the 12 cases in 2025. In November that year, it also allowed his curative petition in the final pending cThe recovery of skulls and bones triggered nationwide outrage and led to the arrest of Koli and Pandher. The case was subsequently transferred from the Uttar Pradesh Police to the CBI amid criticism of the initial investigation. CBI searches around the bungalow and adjoining areas led to the recovery of further human remains.Koli was eventually convicted in 13 cases by the trial court. However, the legal case against him unravelled over the years. In October 2023, the Allahabad High Court acquitted Koli in 12 cases and Pandher in two, citing serious shortcomings in the investigation and questioning the reliability of crucial evidence, including Koli's confession.The Supreme Court upheld Koli's acquittal, setting aside his conviction and ordering his release. The court held that the evidentiary basis for the conviction could not stand after the same evidence had been rejected in the other cases.Pandher, meanwhile, was released from prison in October 2023 after his acquittal.

Article Title: Over 37 lakh appeals pending after Bengal SIR: EC tells Supreme Court
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Friday told the Supreme Court that over 37 lakh appeals against the deletion or inclusion of names in West Bengal electoral rolls under the Special Intensive Revision remain pending.The poll panel told the apex court in its response affidavit that tribunals appointed by the court have disposed of only about 1.02 lakh of the 38.20 lakh appeals filed so far.This comes after a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymala Bagchi and V Mohana sought the poll panel's response to a plea seeking disclosure of assembly constituency-wise data on claims and objections filed by voters whose names were deleted during the SIR exercise.A total of 38,20,683 appeals had been filed against orders relating to the SIR of electoral rolls. Of these, 1,02,231 appeals had been disposed of, leaving 37,18,452 pending, the poll panel said.The affidavit, however, did not provide a break-up of the appeals filed by electors whose names were deleted and those filed against the inclusion of names in the electoral rolls.Prasenjit Bose, who filed the affidavit, claimed that more than 58 lakh electors were excluded during the enumeration phase of the SIR exercise in West Bengal.He added that while 9.64 lakh applications for inclusion (Forms 6 and 6A) and over 99,000 applications for deletion (Form 7) were received during the claims and objections phase, only around 1.82 lakh additions were reflected in the final electoral roll published on February 28.On August 25, the top court directed the Election Commission to submit data on the pendency and disposal of appeals before tribunals challenging exclusion or inclusion in electoral rolls.Observing that these appeals needed to be adjudicated in a time-bound manner, the bench had asked the poll panel to explain what steps were being taken to streamline the mechanism for disposing of pending appeals and how many additional tribunals were required.The EC data submitted to the court showed that 34.13 lakh Form 6 applications had been filed between December 17, 2025, when the draft electoral roll was published, and August 7, 2026.Form 6 is the statutory application for inclusion of a name in the electoral roll.On April 24, the apex court asked the appellate tribunals to give out-of-turn hearings to those who made a case for urgent hearing against deletion from electoral rolls after the SIR.Approximately 700 judicial officers from West Bengal and neighbouring Odisha and Jharkhand were deployed to deal with around 60 lakh claims and objections.Later, the chief justice of the Calcutta high court, on the direction of the top court, set up 19 tribunals headed by former high court chief justices and judges to decide the appeals.
Article Summary: The Election Commission told the Supreme Court that over 37 lakh appeals against the deletion or inclusion of names in West Bengal electoral rolls remain pending. The poll panel told the apex court that tribunals appointed by the court have disposed of only about 1.02 lakh of the 38.20 lakh appeals filed so far.

Article Title: Smooth take off: Pilot handles Punjab turbulence with ‘no CM face’ formula; but can he carry Congress beyond winning line?

Sachin Pilot with Charanjit Singh Channi and Amrinder Singh Raja Warring during a protest to demand justice for the late Gulzar Singh in Chandigarh on Tuesday.

But will Pilot’s truce hold?

Well begun is half done

“No CM face” compromise

PM Modi vs Rahul

NEW DELHI: The Congress in Punjab has finally hit the ground running. Sachin Pilot, who replaced Bhupesh Baghel as the party’s state in-charge, successfully navigated the state unit out of months of internal turmoil and ensured the party’s campaign for the 2027 assembly elections could finally take off.With arch-rivals - former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi and state Congress chief Raja Warring - on board, Pilot led a mega protest demanding the resignation of Punjab finance minister Harpal Cheema, who faces charges of abetment of suicide of a Dalit, Gulzar Singh.The entire state leadership and thousands of party workers marched towards Cheema’s residence. Police used water cannons to stop the protesters’ march. But the point was made. The Congress was finally in action mode.Pilot ensured that Channi and Warring, whose open power tussle has derailed Congress’s Punjab campaign, not only shared the stage but also did a “tense” handshake.Putting up a huge show of unity during the protest, Channi said, "We will fight together." Warring reciprocated. The state Congress chief called Channi and other leaders his 'pagg da lar' (the fold of his turban).Expressing gratitude to party workers for mobilising in such huge numbers at short notice, Pilot assured each one of them that the Congress will always stand by them. The Congress in-charge assured party workers that he was the representative of the high command and would not leave any stone unturned to restore the dignity and honour of every Congress worker.That’s the big question. The Punjab Congress has seen a no-holds-barred battle between Channi and Warring ever since the high command announced on July 1 that Warring would continue as Punjab Congress chief, ignoring Channi’s claims.The announcement triggered immediate protests from Channi’s supporters. They demanded that Channi should be projected as the party’s CM face in the assembly elections. What followed left the Congress leadership red-faced. From war or words to slogan-shouting at party meetings, the wide split in the state unit was out in the open. The Congress sent Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel to firefight, but he was also singed in the crossfire. Channi camp leaders accused him of siding with Warring.Pilot, who was then air-dashed to Punjab to set the house in order, has passed his maiden test. But assembly elections in the state are still at least 5 months away. Holding the rival factions together till then will indeed be a daunting challenge for the former Rajasthan deputy chief minister.So, how did Pilot cross the first hurdle smoothly? What did he do differently, which Bhupesh Baghel couldn’t?Former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel was sent to Punjab in February this year. The Congress in Punjab then was a deeply divided house. Baghel worked hard on the ground to bridge differences between the state leaders. But on July 1, when the Congress high command announced to continue with Raja Warring as the state Congress president and made Channi the head of the campaign committee, the rebellion in the state unit came out in the open.Channi’s supporters openly opposed the decision. When Baghel reinforced the leadership structure and ruled out any change, the rebels openly protested and even raised slogans against him.Baghel tried to pacify the rebels by announcing that Punjab elections would be fought under the leadership of Rahul Gandhi and no state leader would be projected as CM face. But the rebels had lost his trust and refused to budge.With the rebels refusing to relent and their open infighting embarrassing the party leadership, the Congress high command decided to do a course correction to set its house in order.Baghel was shifted out, Pilot was brought in with a clear message: Congress would contest the 2027 assembly elections under collective leadership, and Rahul Gandhi would be the face of the campaign. This was a half-way compromise. The party leadership relented on Baghel but refused to budge on replacing Warring - at least for now.Warring was handpicked by the Congress high command to lead the Punjab unit after the party’s rout in the 2017 assembly elections - which saw the grand-old-party reduced to 17 assembly seats - its worst-ever performance in the state.So, Pilot has crossed the first hurdle. But at what cost? Congress’s decision to fight the Punjab assembly elections under collective leadership, with Rahul Gandhi as the face of the campaign, may have at best delayed the inevitable power tussle.But it creates another challenge for the party. Much of the Congress’s success in the state till now has been driven by a strong local leadership - Captain Amarinder Singh, who is now with the BJP.The AAP has already announced to contest the upcoming assembly elections under the leadership of Bhagwant Singh Mann. Arvind Kejriwal, who is the face of AAP has largely worked from behind the scenes - planning and strategising for the Punjab challenge. For the Akalis, Sukhbir Singh Badal is the undisputed leader and the party’s campaign revolves around him.That leaves us with the BJP and the Congress.The Congress decision to contest Punjab assembly elections with Rahul Gandhi as the party’s face makes the upcoming electoral contest interesting, and perhaps also challenging for the party.The BJP has already launched an aggressive campaign for Punjab with Prime Minister Narendra Modi leading the party’s campaign. PM Modi has already held two rallies in the poll-bound state and has announced a slew of development projects. As the campaign progresses, we will see the Prime Minister go all out against BJP’s political opponents. The BJP, which is in the process of building the party in the state, also has no visible local leadership. It has acquired quite a few prominent leaders from AAP and Congress, but it is unlikely any of them would be projected as the CM face. BJP’s campaigns in states are mostly centralised, with all top leaders campaigning for the party and PM Modi leading the charge. Punjab should be no exception.And that is what should worry the Congress. The fight to conquer Punjab could well become another PM Modi vs Rahul contest. In several such direct contests in the past, the Congress has struggled. However, Punjab could be different. The BJP, for a greater part of its existence in the state, has played second fiddle to the Akalis.The BJP has announced a solo contest in 2027 elections.For the Congress, Punjab has been one of the happiest hunting grounds. Despite the haunting memories of Operation Blue Star and the anti-Sikh killings, Punjab has voted for the Congress. Now, it is over to Pilot to take the Congress beyond the winning line.
Article Summary: Sachin Pilot replaced Bhupesh Baghel as the party’s state in-charge. Pilot led a mega protest demanding the resignation of Punjab finance minister Harpal Cheema, who faces charges of abetment of suicide of a Dalit, Gulzar Singh.

Article Title: Mamata gets 'footballer', but can she win TMC 'khela'? Maharashtra has a red-card warning
Article Text:
Mamata Banerjee faction got 'football player' as its symbol.

Mamata Banerjee is now fighting to save her own party name and symbol.

They do not know that I cannot leave TMC. It will always be with me until I leave this world. Absolutely dirty game, but we are also ready to fight it out. I want the BJP to go from India. We want solidarity in INDIA alliance. Mamata Banerjee

What Shiv Sena and NCP cases tell us

The timeline of TMC split.

The 'new' Mamata party

They had said beforehand, 'naam bhi rakhne doonga, nishaan bhi nahi rakhne doonga' (Neither let you keep the name nor the symbol). Who are these people? They are in power today; they might not be in power tomorrow. They should understand their limitations. Mamata Banerjee

Nandigram changes the bypoll test

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For 28 years, TMC has been Mamata Banerjee and Mamata Banerjee has been TMC in West Bengal; the two are almost synonymous with each other. And for voters, the political shorthand for Mamata Banerjee has been almost absurdly simple: two flowers on grass.Now, that shorthand has been taken away.The Election Commission on Friday allotted Mamata's faction a new name - 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress', with a football player as its symbol. The rival Arup Roy faction will contest as 'Democratic Trinamool Congress', with an 'envelope' as its symbol. The decision follows the commission's September 17 order freezing the original All India Trinamool Congress name and its reserved 'flowers and grass' symbol for the upcoming bypolls.But the EC's interim arrangement is only the first chapter. The substantive question of who gets the original TMC name and symbol will have to be decided under Paragraph 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.And here, the story might look familiar.The same movie was played out twice in Maharashtra in recent years, first with the Shiv Sena and then with the Nationalist Congress Party.When Shiv Sena split between Uddhav Thackeray and Eknath Shinde in 2022, the EC first froze the party's 'bow and arrow' symbol and allotted separate interim identities to the two factions.In its February 2023 decision, the commission eventually recognised the Shinde faction as the Shiv Sena and allowed it to use the original name and symbol.The NCP followed a similar path. After Ajit Pawar's rebellion in July 2023, the EC decided in February 2024 that the faction led by Sharad Pawar had a weaker numerical claim, while Ajit Pawar's group had superior support in the organisational and legislative wings. It consequently recognised Ajit Pawar's faction as the NCP and allowed it to use the party's 'clock' symbol. The EC order specifically recorded that the Ajit Pawar group had "far superior numerical support" in the organisational and legislative wings.That is a crucial part of the precedent for the ongoing TMC dispute.The conclusion from the Maharashtra cases may be that the EC followed the majority of legislators. The legal position is more nuanced. Paragraph 15 allows the election commission to examine rival claims through the party's organisational structure as well as its legislative strength.In its May 11, 2023 Constitution Bench judgment in Subhash Desai vs Principal Secretary, Governor of Maharashtra, the Supreme Court held that the EC need not determine a party's identity solely through the numerical strength of its MLAs or MPs while adjudicating a dispute under Paragraph 15 of the Symbols Order. The court said the EC could consider the majority in the organisational wing, the party constitution and, where appropriate, "any other appropriate test", underlining that a split among legislators is not necessarily the same as a split in the political party itself.The observation is particularly relevant to the TMC case, where the eventual contest could involve competing claims over the party's organisational structure and not just a headcount of elected representatives. The Supreme Court, however, did not itself decide which faction should receive the Shiv Sena's name and symbol, leaving the merits of that EC decision to separate proceedings.That distinction could matter considerably in the TMC case.The Shiv Sena and NCP rebels who ultimately secured the original party identities had substantial support among sitting legislators. The TMC's internal arithmetic, however, has to be examined on its own terms.The 2026 assembly election setback changed the party's internal arithmetic sharply. Its tally fell from 215 of 294 seats in 2021 to 80, and within weeks, 58 MLAs backed expelled leader Ritabrata Banerjee as their legislature party leader. He was subsequently recognised as leader of the opposition, while the rebel camp rejected Mamata's nominee, Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay.The revolt then spread to Parliament, with 20 Lok Sabha MPs led by Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar joining the NCPI and backing the BJP-led NDA. The TMC challenged their move before the Lok Sabha speaker and sought their disqualification. What began as a post-election leadership challenge had thus expanded into a contest over control of the party's legislative and parliamentary wings.Mamata Banerjee, however, remains the founder and central political figure of the organisation, and her camp's claim is not based only on her position as party leader but also on its organisational and electoral support.The names allotted on Friday were revealing because neither faction chose to abandon the Trinamool identity. Mamata's camp was given 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress', while the rival Arup Roy camp became 'Democratic Trinamool Congress'. Both were, in different ways, laying claim to continuity with the party Mamata Banerjee founded on January 1, 1998.The distinction lies in the source of legitimacy each side is emphasising. The rebels' use of 'Democratic' fits their argument that the TMC's organisational functioning should be more representative and less centred around one leader. Mamata's faction, meanwhile, has effectively put the founder's name where the old party identity used to be, making 'Mamata' part of its temporary electoral brand. That is particularly striking for a party whose political identity has been inseparable from its founder for almost three decades.The football-player symbol allotted to Mamata's faction also carries its own political resonance in Bengal. Football has long had a deep cultural presence in the state, but there is also a direct connection to the TMC's campaign vocabulary: 'Khela Hobe', the slogan that became a defining part of Mamata's 2021 assembly campaign against the BJP.The symbol does not automatically recreate that campaign, but it gives the Mamata faction a ready-made visual association at a time when it has lost the party symbol voters have known for nearly three decades.The test, however, has now changed in a rather dramatic way for the Mamata faction.Mamata faction's candidate, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew her nomination from the Nandigram contest altogether, a day before the deadline. Her withdrawal came minutes after she met West Bengal chief minister and BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari, although the circumstances surrounding the meeting and her decision remain a matter of political speculation.Mamata Banerjee later announced in a press conference that her party will now back the Congress candidate in Nandigram, and mentioned that the decision was taken "for the greater interest of the nation" and to strengthen the INDIA bloc."Rahul Gandhi rang me up yesterday, Arvind Kejriwal also expressed solidarity; we will all fight together against BJP. We will support Congress in the Nandigram bypoll to strengthen the INDIA bloc," Mamata said. The Congress candidate, however, was also arrested by the cops late in the evening in a land-grab case.That makes the October 6 bypolls a very different test from the one that appeared possible 24 hours earlier. The Mamata faction will now not be testing its new 'football-player' identity in Nandigram, but instead, ask its supporters to transfer their support to a Congress candidate, even as the rival TMC faction contests the seat under its own new identity.The political significance is difficult to miss. At precisely the moment when the EC has stripped Mamata's faction of the old TMC name and symbol and given it a new identity, the faction is now out of a direct fight in Nandigram, a constituency that carries an unusually strong personal history for both Mamata and Suvendu Adhikari.Nandigram was where Mamata lost to Adhikari in the 2021 assembly election, after making the constituency the centrepiece of her campaign. Adhikari, who had moved from the TMC to the BJP before that election, defeated her by a narrow margin in a contest that became one of the defining episodes of Bengal politics. He subsequently retained Nandigram while also winning Bhowanipore, which he vacated to retain Nandigram, necessitating the October 6 bypoll.The EC may eventually decide who owns the TMC name and symbol, but the October 6 bypolls will offer the first test of how much of the old Trinamool identity survives without 'flowers and grass'. In Rejinagar, the football player and envelope will face each other directly; in Nandigram, Mamata's decision to back Congress will test whether her political support can travel even when her own new party name and symbol are not on the ballot.
Article Summary: The Election Commission on Friday allotted Mamata's faction a new name - 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress' But the substantive question of who gets the original TMC name and symbol will have to be decided. The same movie was played out twice in Maharashtra in recent years, first with Shiv Sena and then with the Nationalist Congress Party.

Article Title: Kashmir cracks walnut success code, turns to medium-sized, grafted trees
Article Text:
A street vendor sells walnuts on the occasion of the Sayar festival, in Mandi on Wednesday. (ANI Photo)

KOKERNAG: In Gohan village, around 100km south of Srinagar, Shabir Ahmad was among many harvesting walnuts from a towering tree. The work has become increasingly difficult. “My back aches now,” Ahmad said. J&K produces 3.5 lakh tonnes of walnuts annually, around 90% of the country’s total output.Like other villagers, Ahmad had no safety gear and he was proud of it. “We have been doing it for centuries,” said Ahmad, also a clerk at a local court. However, the bravado doesn’t help in harvesting seasons. Dr. Mohd Yaqoob Bhat, a surgeon at Paras Hospital in Srinagar, said Valley healthcare units treat dozens of patients each year after falls from walnut trees, some with serious spinal injuries. “There is no mechanism to address the issue,” Bhat said.Ahmad’s younger brother sold one walnut for one rupee and no two fruits are similar. For generations, Kashmir’s walnut trees have been grown from seeds. J&K and Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology (SKUAST) are now promoting medium-sized, grafted walnut trees to bring greater uniformity and help the produce compete globally amid competition from soft-shelled varieties grown in California and Chile.The initiative aims to replace scattered plantations with organised orchards of known varieties, allowing farmers to grow more trees in the same area and produce walnuts more consistent in size and color.J&K has about 80,000 hectares under walnut cultivation, most of it made up of seedling-origin trees. “When someone plants a walnut seed in the ground, whatever grows becomes a tree. Every tree is a variety of its own,” Ashfaq A. Pandit, professor and head of fruit science at SKUAST, said. This natural variation, once considered an advantage, has become a challenge in the modern market where buyers seek consistent produce.Traditional walnut trees can take about 15 years to bear fruit without using pesticides. Unlike traditional seedling-origin trees, grafted walnuts belong to known varieties.Imtiyaz Ahmad Lone, professor and head of SKUAST’s Walnut Research Centre, said the university released new walnut cultivars and grafting-based cultivation had spread over nearly 90,000 hectares despite lack of subsidies.Farmers argued, however, that the grafted varieties are no match for the traditional Kashmiri walnut. “It is no match in taste. The new varieties are brittle, tasteless. They are a no-show,” Mohammad Sultan, a Pulwama farmer in the business for 50 years, said.Researchers differed. Lone pointed out that grafted trees have early bearing, give faster returns as orchards and nut quality are uniform. “They have higher productivity and better export potential. There is a gradual opportunity to replace unproductive seedling trees,” he said.The transition has impacted walnut woodcraft industries. Walnut trees cannot be cut in J&K without govt permission. The matter was debated in the assembly in March when CM Omar Abdullah opposed a bill allowing landowners to cut walnut trees on private property. Omar defended the restrictions, saying the law served a broader purpose of conserving walnut and chinar trees.
Article Summary: J&K produces 3.5 lakh tonnes of walnuts annually, around 90% of the country’s total output. J&K and Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology (SKUAST) are promoting medium-sized, grafted walnut trees.

Article Title: 'Will take all necessary actions': India's stern warning amid reports of Bangladesh reviewing 101 bilateral pacts
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: India on Friday said it would take 'all necessary actions' to safeguard its interests after reports that Bangladesh is reviewing 101 agreements and memorandums of understanding signed with New Delhi during the previous Awami League government.Responding to news agency ANI, at the ministry of external affairs’ bi-weekly briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said New Delhi had not received any formal communication from Dhaka on the review.“We also have seen some media reports on this matter, but nothing has been conveyed to us officially. Obviously, India will take all necessary actions to protect its interests,” Jaiswal said.Bangladesh’s ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has said the agreements are being examined with the country’s national interests in mind. chief Whip Nurul Islam Moni said last week, “We are reviewing the agreements that mean 101 MoUs and you will get its (review) result soon.”The review covers arrangements signed under former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League government. Among the areas under scrutiny are agreements linked to the use of Chattogram and Mongla ports, connectivity and other bilateral projects. Dhaka has not announced a blanket cancellation of the agreements.The developments come as India-Bangladesh ties face scrutiny over trade, transit, energy, border management and water-sharing issues. India has previously extended more than $7 billion through Lines of Credit for infrastructure projects in Bangladesh, while bilateral arrangements have also enabled the movement of Indian cargo through Bangladeshi ports.Water-sharing remains another key issue. The 1996 Ganga Water Sharing Treaty is due to expire in December 2026, while the long-pending Teesta agreement remains unresolved.On Friday, Jaiswal said existing mechanisms for discussions on shared rivers remained operational.“In the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty between Bangladesh and India, we have the Joint Rivers Commission mechanism to discuss all water-related issues. Technical-level meetings on water matters continue to be held,” he said.India and Bangladesh share 54 rivers, Jaiswal said, adding that water-related issues are handled through the Joint Rivers Commission and other established bilateral mechanisms.The review of the 101 agreements is now expected to provide a clearer indication of whether Dhaka intends to retain, amend or renegotiate specific arrangements.
Article Summary: India says it will take 'all necessary actions' to safeguard its interests. Bangladesh is reviewing 101 agreements and memorandums of understanding. The review covers arrangements signed under former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League government. Among the areas under scrutiny are agreements linked to the use of Chattogram and Mongla ports.

Article Title: 'It can't be that Hindi will not be taught in Tamil Nadu', SC tells state during hearing on Navodaya schools
Article Text:
‘Chennai shouldn’t alienate Delhi’: SC tells Tamil Nadu to reconsider opposition to Navodaya schools

Tamil Nadu raises language concerns

Court stresses cooperative federalism

State raises financial concerns

Supreme Court refuses to recall land direction

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Tamil Nadu government to comply with its December 15, 2025 order to identify land in every district for establishing Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas, while urging the state and Centre to resolve their differences over the schools through dialogue.A bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and Augustine George Masih also questioned Tamil Nadu's opposition to the three-language policy followed by Navodaya schools and said the state should not view the establishment of the centrally funded institutions as a threat to its existing education system."You have to change your mindset, it can’t be that Hindi will not be taught in the soil of Tamil Nadu," Justice Nagarathna observed during the hearing.The bench also said the people in Chennai should not alienate those in Delhi while stressing the need for cooperative federalism."We are saying in addition to all the good things you’re doing in your State, having something in addition will not bring down your standards. Coming from Delhi, will not lower the standards of Chennai. People in Chennai should not alienate Delhi and vice versa," the Court said.The court granted Tamil Nadu three more months to identify suitable land in each district and directed representatives of the state and Central governments to hold further discussions on the policy for establishing the schools.The matter has been posted for December 14.The case relates to Tamil Nadu's challenge to a Madras High Court direction to establish Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district.Navodaya schools are centrally funded, co-educational residential schools run by the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti under the Union Ministry of Education. Tamil Nadu has opposed their establishment, among other reasons, because the schools follow a three-language policy that includes Hindi, while the state follows a two-language policy.Senior Advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for Tamil Nadu, told the court that the state's objection was not to schools or the teaching of Hindi as such, but to the language policy associated with the Navodaya scheme."It is against the State policy. It supersedes Tamil. This kind of unification is not the purport of the Constitution. It is not a Central government school. It is a school run by a society. There is an adamancy that Hindi must predominate."Justice Nagarathna said the language issue could be discussed between the Centre and the state."If you want Tamil as a second language, it is a matter which can be considered," the Judge said, asking the state Secretary to speak to the corresponding Central government Secretary.Gupta said discussions had already taken place but the Centre had remained adamant about Hindi. He nevertheless agreed to another round of consultations.Tamil Nadu also argued that the judiciary could not compel a state to adopt an optional Central government policy through a mandamus.Gupta submitted that education is in the Concurrent List and that Tamil Nadu has constitutional authority to frame its own education policy. He also argued that the Navodaya scheme was not compulsory.Justice Nagarathna questioned the consequences of individual states refusing to accept Central policies."Education is in the Concurrent List. There has to be cooperative federalism. If each State says that I don't accept your policy, what will happen?" the Judge asked.The bench said Tamil Nadu could continue running its own institutions and following its own syllabus, while Navodaya schools would provide an additional educational option.The court also rejected the argument that the establishment of Navodaya schools would lower Tamil Nadu's educational standards."We are not alienating you and we are not alienating them. Some more type of schools come in your state also which will only enhance the high standard which we are aware of. This is not going to lower your standards. If Navodaya schools were going to lower the standard of education in Tamil Nadu we would have said that irrespective of what you would have said. That is not the case here. It will provide more opportunity," Justice Nagarathna told Gupta."Ultimately everybody must work together," Justice Nagarathna said.Tamil Nadu also raised financial concerns, submitting that the Centre had promised to release Rs 5,000 crore for education but had not done so.Gupta argued that the state could not take on additional financial liabilities when funds under existing schemes had allegedly not been released.Additional Solicitor General KM Nataraj, appearing for the Centre, submitted that the state's primary requirement under the scheme was to provide land, while construction and other expenses would be borne by the Central government.Nataraj said the scheme was at an early stage and construction would take several years, during which the language-related differences could be addressed through discussions.Gupta, however, said around 30 acres of land would be required in each district and that identifying land before deciding whether to accept the policy would create difficulties.The bench clarified that it was not directing the state to acquire land immediately, but only to identify suitable land in its government plan.The Supreme Court had in December 2025 directed Tamil Nadu to identify land required for establishing Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district within six weeks. The state subsequently sought recall of the order.On Thursday, the bench declined to recall the direction and instead granted the state three months to comply.In its order, the bench recorded that Tamil Nadu had cited the change in government and lack of material progress in discussions with the Centre as reasons for non-compliance."Be that as it may, we direct the petitioner to comply with our order of 15.12.2025 in so far as identification of the land necessary to establish the school in each district," the order stated.The bench also directed the Centre and Tamil Nadu to continue discussions on the policy while the state works on identifying the land.Advocates G Priyadarshini and Rahul Shyam Bhandari, appearing for Kumari Maha Sabha, the petitioner before the High Court, argued that Tamil Nadu could not deny students access to free education through Navodaya schools."The Court should not get into this debate," Gupta said during the hearing.Justice Nagarathna responded: "That perception that you are surrendering to the central govt should not be there."
Article Summary: Supreme Court orders Tamil Nadu to comply with its December 15, 2025 order to identify land in every district for Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas. Justices BV Nagarathna and Augustine George Masih also questioned Tamil Nadu's opposition to the three-language policy. The bench also said the people in Chennai should not alienate those in Delhi while stressing the need for cooperative federalism.

Article Title: MHA cites internal security issues to defend FCRA tweak
Article Text:
Bill doesn’t regulate charity, but flow of foreign funds intosovereign space, JPC Informed

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Amid the charge from the opposition that Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill targets institutions run by minorities, especially Christians, Union home ministry asserted Friday that the amendments do not regulate charity but the entry of foreign money into a "sovereign space", which Centre is fully entitled to protect, and emphasised the law at its core is a "national-security" legislation.A team of MHA officials led by home secretary Govind Mohan briefed the joint committee of Parliament - which is scrutinising the bill and held its first meeting - on different facets as it faced questions from MPs, with Mohan insisting the bill is not against any community, sources aware of the details said.He said concerns over national interest, internal security and law and order are the main drivers of the bill. It was introduced by govt in Parliament's budget session and sent to the committee for scrutiny amid stiff protests from opposition parties and Christian groups, who had met home minister Amit Shah to convey their concerns.After the meeting, the panel's chairperson, Sanjay Jaiswal, expressed confidence that it would be able to submit its report in the winter session of Parliament.MPs from BJP-led NDA and opposition parties presented conflicting views.BJP's Nishikant Dubey suggested India had a history of foreign money being used to influence issues of national interest and asked why Ford Foundation was allotted prime property in Lodhi Estate when over 1,400 NGOs linked to foreign funding were closed down under different laws before FCRA was enacted in 1976.Rockefeller Foundation was a key financial support behind an elite cultural and intellectual organisation in central Delhi, he said.Sources said DMK's P Wilson reiterated the charge that the amendments target Christian groups, which make up the majority of religious organisations with an FCRA licence, and was supported by other opposition MPs. Some alleged that these organisations were being targeted as they had empowered Dalits and women in south India.Opposition MPs slammed the proposed amendments as draconian, saying even if an organisation surrendered its FCRA licence, it still allowed assets to be seized.Jaiswal, sources said, flagged protests against the Kudankulam nuclear plant in TN and Sardar Sarovar Dam in Gujarat. BJP circles have argued that foreign-funded NGOs tried to disrupt the two critical projects of national interest under the veneer of environmental concerns.According to data shared by MHA, TN has the highest number of organisations with FCRA registration (2,102), followed by Maharashtra (1,578), Karnataka (1,355) and Delhi (1,218). Foreign contribution increased to Rs 22,974 crore in 2024-25 from Rs 17,832 crore in 2015-16.Out of the total foreign contribution received in 2024-25, 57% (Rs 13,071 crore) was for social purposes, 30% (Rs 6,933 crore) for educational, and only 8% (Rs 11,841 crore) for religious. Under the head of religious purpose, 73% went to Christian groups followed by 17.8% for Hindu organisations, with a little over 1% to Muslims. US and UK at Rs 12,113 crore and Rs 2,414 crore respectively were the two highest contributors.
Article Summary: Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill is being scrutinised by Parliament's joint committee of MPs. Union home ministry says the amendments do not regulate charity but the entry of foreign money into a "sovereign space" It emphasised the law at its core is a "national-security" legislation.

Article Title: SC questions alcohol prohibition law, points to 5 'evils'

NEW DELHI: Questioning the efficacy of prohibition, Supreme Court Friday pointed to five "evils" associated with the ban on liquor - revenue loss, money spent on its enforcement, corruption in police, illegal distilling, and result-ant drug menace - while also referring to a number of hooch tragedies in Gujarat and other states over the years.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said this while quashing Rules 18A and 18B of Maharashtra Poisons Rules restricting purchase of methanol and making it mandatory to add bitterant and colourant to it before selling to non-drug manufacturers. The rules were framed following the deaths of 93 people from spurious liquor containing methanol in Mumbai in 1991.While allowing the plea of various chemical manufacturing companies, including Indian Chemical Council, the bench dwelled upon the efficacy of the prohibition policy. The court said recent hooch tragedies in Bhavnagar (Gujarat) and Sagar (MP), which claimed 13 and 15 lives respectively, were a reminder for the authorities to wake up and act."History bears eloquent testimony to the fact that complete alcohol ban often drives the liquor trade underground, increasing the prevalence of unregulated, lethal brews. The state of Gujarat has a strict prohibition policy... It has witnessed at least 10 major mass hooch tragedies since the state's formation and independence, claiming the lives of over 600 people," the bench said.SC rejected Maharashtra govt's plea and said the rules had no rational nexus with the objective sought to be achieved to prevent hooch tragedies. The court said it was not doubting the intention of the state but intention solely would not pass the test of manifest arbitrariness."The state failed to indicate that this practice of putting such additives would discourage or rather dissuade continuous usage of methanol or affect its chemical composition so it cannot be used in making spurious liquor. Further, the state has also failed to indicate how mixing of the additives would definitively prevent deaths. Another question that is left unanswered is how the respondent plans to prevent manufacturing of spurious liquor by the use of other adulterants," the bench said.
Article Summary: Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said this while quashing Rules 18A and 18B of Maharashtra Poisons Rules. The rules were framed following the deaths of 93 people from spurious liquor containing methanol in Mumbai in 1991.

Article Title: When the mullai refused to bloom
Article Text:
“Mullaiyum Pooththiyo, Ollaiyur Naade?”

“Vaiyaththul Vaazhvaangu Vaazhpavan Vaanuraiyum

Theyvaththul Vaikkap Padum.”

He embodied it.

On the day Pappaiah sir was laid to rest, there was orderliness at the church, and all the way to the burial ground. But as the van entered the cemetery, a sea of cameras took over. His family, and those of us from his intimate literary circle, could not go near him. I could not get a last glimpse the doyen of Tamil Pattimandram and connoisseur of literature. He left without our goodbye.On our way to the airport, a flower vendor tapped on our car window. In her hands was a bunch of maruda malli. The flowers looked wilted. A Sangam poem by Kudavayil Keerathanar came to my mind. After mourning Sathan, his patron, the poet, on entering Ollaiyur and seeing the mullai blooming, asks the flower why, when no one in the grieving land will wear it:I looked at the wilted flowers and thought: How could flowers bloom in Madurai on the day a great son of its soil was being laid to rest?Grief has a physical weight. At first, memories flood. Then life resumes its ordinary rhythm, only to ambush us at unexpected moments. Some of us had the rare privilege of spending hours with him, seeing the man beyond the stage—his humility.Years ago, when I joined his team and the celebrated Pattimandram on Sun TV , a few jealous voices tried to push me out. A sentence I had casually uttered was relayed to him as an “objectionable” remark, and I was told that affected parties might send a legal notice to me and to him as moderator.My life on stage was over, I thought. But he looked at the person who had brought him the news and said, “It looks like you are the affected party who has staged this.”That day I learnt something precious: he could be formidable when protecting those entrusted to him. He was not merely a judge of debates; he was a discerning judge of people.I learnt about simplicity from him too. At functions, the rich and powerful would surround him for photographs. But his eyes would seek the drivers, cleaning women and security guards standing at a distance, and he would walk towards them and ask for a picture.His greatest literary contribution was taking the Thirukkural into ordinary homes. For more than seven years, he travelled almost every week from Madurai to Chennai, often by train, to record a Kural a day for Sun TV, beginning with his unforgettable, “Loving mothers, revered elders and sweet children.” Ancient wisdom entered countless contemporary lives.I met him at Sivakasi just five days before he passed away. He was as vibrant as ever. The topic was Gen Z. We wondered how he would connect with them. He did more than connect. He spoke their language and gave his verdict in their favour.He seemed to be passing on the mantle.He went home that day and never returned to the stage.No prolonged hospitalisation. No dependence. A dignified life, followed by a dignified death.And in death, he brought alive Kural 50:One who lives an ordained life in this world, Is placed among the divine.Pappaiah sir did not merely explain that Kural.
Article Summary: Pappaiah sir was the doyen of Tamil Pattimandram and connoisseur of literature. His greatest literary contribution was taking the Thirukkural into ordinary homes. For more than seven years, he travelled almost every week from Madurai to Chennai, often by train, to record a Kural a day.

Article Title: 25% youths in 250 districts not in education or jobs: Survey
Article Text:
The situation is of particular concern in northernIndia (Representative image)

Lowest unemployment rates across India

NEW DELHI: In nearly 250 districts, more than 25% youth (15-29 age group) are neither engaged in any productive work, nor are they pursuing education or any sort of training for work, highlighting a gap in human capital utilisation.The situation is of particular concern in northern India, especially in states such as Bihar, UP, Haryana, Punjab and West Bengal, where nearly two-thirds of districts have around a quarter of the young population categorised as NEET (not in employment, education or training), showed the first-ever district-level periodic labour force survey (PLFS) for 2025, released by statistics ministry Friday.In Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Assam and Telangana in nearly half the districts, 25% young population is categorised as NEET (not in employment, education or training). A recent Niti Aayog report pegged the number of NEET youth in the country at nearly nine crore, with govt clarifying that these people cannot be crudely termed as unemployed.In around 25 districts, NEET is below 10%, including Kabirdham, Rajnandgaon and Uttar Baster Kanker in Chhattisgarh; Chamba in Himachal Pradesh; Ernakulam in Kerala; and Mandla in Madhya Pradesh. Nabarangpur in Odisha had the lowest NEET rate of 4.1%.The ministry's report covered around 600 districts in major states and UTs. In some cases, it clubbed a few adjoining districts and treated them as a single unit.Generally, high unemployment rate among youth is attributed to their participation in education or their engagement with skilling or vocational programmes. NEET, however, represents those people who are not enrolled anywhere with any educational institution and have also withdrawn from the labour force altogether. This is either due to them attending to domestic unpaid duties, care work in the case of women or those who have stopped looking for work due to no suitable work being available, or in some cases, preparing for exams or having leisure. For young women, nearly three-fourth of total districts surveyed recorded a NEET rate of more than 25%, highlighting the burden of unpaid domestic chores and societal expectations.
Article Summary: In nearly 250 districts, more than 25% youth (15-29 age group) are neither engaged in any productive work, nor are they pursuing education. The situation is of particular concern in northern India, especially in states such as Bihar, UP, Haryana, Punjab and West Bengal.

Article Title: Presumption of guilt doesn't make prosecution case 'gospel truth': SC
Article Text:
A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and NV Anjaria gave this ruling

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a judgment that will impact as many as nine penal laws, Supreme Court has ruled that the stringent provisions of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act providing for presumption of guilt of the accused must not persuade trial courts to believe the prosecution's case to be the "gospel truth".A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and N V Anjaria gave this ruling while setting aside concurrent judgments of a Delhi court and Delhi HC convicting a man, whom a woman had falsely accused of sexually assaulting her minor daughter in a Kalkaji slum in south Delhi in 2015. It said the accusation was part of a long-standing feud over water the woman had with him.The bench said both the trial court and HC appeared to have been swayed by the presumption of guilt provision in Pocso Act and overlooked glaring discrepancies and loopholes in the mother's testimony despite these being highlighted by the accused during cross-examination. Writing the judgment, Justice Anjaria said presumption of guilt in Pocso Act did not operate to eliminate evidence standing in favour of the accused.The statutory presumptions cannot be read to mean that the prosecution version is liable to be treated as gospel truth in every case," he said.The presumptive provision cannot unburden courts from "discharging their essential duty to analyse the evidence on record in light of the features emerging in a particular case", he added.This ruling will potentially impact provisions of presumption of guilt against the accused, or casting reverse burden on them, in eight other laws - Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, Prevention of Corruption Act, Wild Life (Protection) Act, Essential Commodities Act, Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, Customs Act, Foreign Exchange Management Act, and Negotiable Instruments Act, which were specifically mentioned in the 42-page judgment.Justices Mishra and Anjaria said, "The court should not mechanically accept the ipse dixit of the prosecution riding on the provisions regarding presumption of guilt to give a stamp of approval to every prosecution even if they are absurd or improbable in its story."It said the provision, or the rule of reverse burden requiring the accused to prove his innocence, did not change the rule of standard of proof as normally applied in criminal cases.
Article Summary: Supreme Court rules that the stringent provisions of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act must not persuade trial courts to believe the prosecution's case to be the "gospel truth" A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and N V Anjaria gave this ruling.

Article Title: Scottish Sikh gets bail in 7 NIA cases after 8 years behind bars

British citizen Jagtar Singh Johal, who was granted bail

NEW DELHI/LONDON/BATHINDA: Delhi HC on Friday granted bail to British citizen Jagtar Singh Johal, who is charged with targeted killings and conspiracy linked to Khalistan Liberation Force (KLF), taking note of his “long period of incarceration” and acquittal in one of the cases. News of his bail sparked celebrations at his home in Dumbarton, Scotland, and among UK-based activists who have been campaigning for his release.His brother Gurpreet Singh Johal, a solicitor in Dumbarton, where Johal’s wife Gurpreet Kaur Johal also lives, said, “The past two years have been an expensive rollercoaster, contesting bails at Supreme Court and back to the high court in India. Now, all I can think about is Jagtar walking out of prison. We have waited so long and fought so hard for this moment. Whenever evidence against Jagtar is tested in court, judges find what we’ve said all along, which is that there isn’t any. ”Johal’s MP Douglas McAllister, who has been campaigning for his release, described the news as “amazing”. “Now it’s time to bring him home.”Scotland-born Johal, arrested shortly after his 2017 wedding, was named as an accused in eight cases of attempted murder in Punjab and booked by NIA under UAPA.He was acquitted in one of the cases last year.HC heard Johal’s bail appeals in the remaining seven case together Friday and said, “We find the appellant has remained in custody for more than eight years… Only 40 witnesses have so far been examined and we are informed there are another 123 witnesses whose testimony is yet to be recorded... Trial is certainly not likely to conclude any time soon.”On NIA’s claim Johal was a flight risk as a foreign national, HC ordered Johal to surrender his passport and barred him from joining any WhatsApp group or other social media platform where anti-national material was uploaded or circulated or propagated.It rejected NIA’s claim certain witnesses alleged they were threatened and that, if released, Johal might influence the trial.NIA’s cases against Johal arise from a series of allegedly targeted murders and attempted murders in Ludhiana and Jalandhar in 2016-2017. Two cases pertain to the killing of Amit Sharma, president of Shri Hindu Takhat in Ludhiana in Jan 2017, and the attempted murder of Jagdish Kumar Gagneja, RSS vice-president in Punjab, in Jalandhar in Aug 2016.The probe was transferred from Punjab Police to NIA after the offences were identified to be a part of a “transnational conspiracy”. NIA accused Johal of being an “active member” of the “terrorist gang” KLF.Gurpreet Singh Johal told BBC News, “We are still waiting for the order and a report. We expect he won’t be allowed to leave India without permission... But at last we see some light at the end of the tunnel that he will be at least at liberty.”Noting Johal was acquitted of all charges in one case, he said, “Jagtar is innocent and is arbitrarily detained. There is a lot more that has to be done from UK govt. They have not done enough.”Dan Dolan, deputy executive director of Reprieve, a UK legal rights organisation campaigning for Johal’s release, said, “While this judgment is welcome as Jagtar should not be in prison a day longer, we must now watch closely to ensure this order is actually implemented and not obstructed in any way.”Chris Esdaile, senior legal adviser at REDRESS, a London NGO that pursues legal claims on behalf of survivors of torture around the world that also campaigned for Johal, said, “This is a welcome development but it can’t undo the intolerable suffering caused by nine years of arbitrary detention without a fair and timely resolution.”
Article Summary: Delhi HC on Friday granted bail to British citizen Jagtar Singh Johal. He is charged with targeted killings and conspiracy linked to Khalistan Liberation Force (KLF) News of his bail sparked celebrations at his home in Dumbarton, Scotland, and among UK-based activists.

Article Title: Uri centre meant for cross-LOC trade will be border tourism hub
Article Text:
TFC will now be used for border tourism

SRINAGAR: A trade facilitation centre (TFC) at Salamabad in border town Uri, which once facilitated duty-free, cashless barter trade between J&K and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK), will now be used for border tourism, ending speculation about resumption of trade through the route.A senior tourism department official confirmed the govt had authorised the department to utilise the TFC located in Baramulla district for tourism-related activities. “The larger objective is to use Salamabad as a gateway to the wider Uri border tourism circuit,” the official said. He added that the emphasis will be on “regulated, responsible and curated border tourism”, ensuring that these remain fully aligned with security and administrative requirements.Salamabad TFC, around 100 km north of Srinagar, was originally established for cross-LoC trade. Following the suspension of such trade in 2019, the facility has remained unutilised for its original purpose.After improved relations in 2008, both India and Pakistan decided to allow cross-LoC trade and travel on certain conditions as part of confidence-building measures (CBMs). However, in April 2019, the Centre suspended the facilities saying the trade routes were being misused for funneling illegal weapons, narcotics, and fake currency.“During ongoing investigations of certain cases by NIA, it has been brought out that a significant number of trading concerns engaged in LoC trade are operated by persons closely associated with banned terrorist organisations involved in fuelling terrorism/separatism,” a Union home ministry (MHA) release had said then. The statement also mentioned that some individuals, who had crossed over and joined terror outfits, had opened trading firms in Pakistan.The cross-LoC travel (bus service) and trade were seen as two of the biggest CBMs between the neighbours in decades. Then PM Manmohan Singh flagged off Karwaan-e-Aman (peace caravan), the first cross-LoC bus service that connected Srinagar with Muzaffarabad in PoK, on April 7, 2005.Cross-LoC barter trade began on Oct 21, 2008, through two routes -- Salamabad (Uri)-Muzaffarabad (PoK) and Poonch-Rawalakot (PoK). Traders on either side were permitted to exchange 21 mutually agreed items.Both sides constructed TFCs 5km inside LoC. In J&K, one TFC came up at Salamabad and the other at Chakan da bagh in Jammu’s Poonch district. Trade was allowed through both routes four days a week.
Article Summary: Salamabad TFC, around 100 km north of Srinagar, was originally established for cross-LoC trade. In April 2019, the Centre suspended the facilities saying the trade routes were being misused for funneling illegal weapons, narcotics, and fake currency.

Article Title: Need to state policy intent clearly while notifying rules, guidelines: Official
Article Text:
MoHUA Secretary D Thara

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: There is a need to write the “intent” of policies, regulations and guidelines in brief while notifying them, a move that will bring clarity and communicate what it aims to achieve, suggested D Thara, secretary of newly created department of capital development under the housing and urban affairs ministry.Speaking at a conference of the real estate sector by Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Thara said people making policies often assume a policy has been communicated clearly, only to find that it is interpreted in completely different ways by different stakeholders depending on their interests or perceived gains and losses.She said that communicating an intent is a “very big challenge” for policymakers. “For example, we write a single sentence and we are thinking we have communicated this and then later we found out that it had just the opposite interpretation in some other quarter... So I’m just wondering how do you bring out that clarity as to what is the intent? Intent is more important than what the sentence communicates.Thara said that henceforth her department will adopt the practice of writing a small intent before going on to the real policy prescription. “I think one reform we should all adopt in govt is this,” she addedThe official also urged the real estate developers to work closely with city municipalities to create necessary physical infrastructure for their residential and commercial projects.She also urged builders to focus on rain harvesting, water recycling and sewage treatment among other critical facilities.“Every development creates an interaction with the larger urban environment, and we need to understand and mitigate the externalities that construction can create for the city,” she said. Calling for a new public-private paradigm in urban development, Thara asked real estate developers to work more closely with municipal agencies and assess the impact of every project beyond its boundaries - from the water it displaces and the sewage it generates, to the energy it consumes and the infrastructure it requires.
Article Summary: D Thara is secretary of newly created department of capital development under housing and urban affairs ministry.
