CHANDIGARH: Ending a prolonged standoff with state employees, the Bhagwant Mann government on Friday announced relief for around eight lakh employees and pensioners, increasing the Dearness Allowance (DA) by 8 per cent.The decision followed a meeting held here between chief minister Bhagwant Mann and representatives of employee and pensioners' organisations.Ministers Aman Arora and Baljeet Kaur, chief secretary KAP Sinha, secretary general administration KK Yadav and others were also present.After the meeting, Gurnam Singh Virk, president of Punjab State Ministerial Services Union, said the enhanced DA will be given from October 1.He said, regarding various other issues, the government has also assured them that these will be discussed soon.The deadlock began August 27 when over three lakh government employees went on a statewide strike by availing mass casual leave, pressing the state government to accept their various demands, including release of their pending 18 per cent Dearness Allowance.An official statement quoting Bhagwant Mann said the move reflects his government's commitment to the welfare and dignity of employees, whom he described as the backbone of the state's administrative machinery.The chief minister also announced compulsory monthly meetings with employee representatives to address genuine issues, postings for women employees within 40 kilometres of their homes, and highlighting that around 70,000 government jobs have been provided through a transparent and corruption-free process.Women employees should not have to choose between their career and their family responsibilities. This increase will start reflecting with the October salary"."We also discussed long-pending issues inherited from previous governments, including the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), salary during the probation period, and issues concerning ASHA and Mid-Day Meal workers. We will meet again in the first week of October to work towards a permanent resolution of these longstanding issues."There is no distance between our government and employees. We will resolve every issue through mutual dialogue. We will continue to work together for Punjab's progress," he said.Emphasising that the welfare, dignity and legitimate concerns of government employees remain a priority for his government, Mann said, "As per the decision, two instalments of 4 per cent each will be released to employees and pensioners, with the benefit to be reflected in their salaries from October 1. "The chief minister said, "The government understands the responsibilities shouldered by its employees and the pressures they face in their personal and professional lives.""A happy employee is a productive employee and I believe that when an employee works with satisfaction, dignity and peace of mind, the entire system performs better and the people receive better services..."."The state government has an open mind towards the genuine demands of employees and pensioners and these issues will be examined sympathetically and in accordance with the applicable rules, financial implications and legal position."He said the government will examine various long-pending demands, including "the demand for a 2.59 pension multiplication factor, restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS), restoration of various allowances, implementation of Assured Career Progression (ACP), issues relating to the 2015 and 2020 letters concerning the probation period, generalization of court decisions and others.""No genuine issue concerning employees is being ignored and the government will examine each matter with an open and sympathetic approach. Article Title: Stringent ‘red entry’ clause in land revenue record proposed to curb farm fires in Delhi-NCR and adjoining areas
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Seeking to make rules to act against stubble burning cases more stringent, the Centre has proposed to mark land revenue records of erring farmers with a ‘red entry’ for a period of 15 months that may potentially be much more consequential than just an existing fine.The rules, once finalised, will be applicable in Delhi, Punjab, Haryana and National Capital Region (NCR) of Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. Stubble burning episodes in these areas lead to a substantial increase in the level of air pollution in Delhi-NCR every winter.Though the draft rules to this effect, notified by the Union environment ministry, have not spelt out the consequences of the ‘red entry’ mark in the land revenue record, officials hinted that they may potentially disallow farmers to sell their lands and stop them from availing benefits of govt schemes. They may even include restrictions on getting registered for selling their produce at minimum support price (MSP) at designated ‘mandis’ for a certain period.The proposed rules, which will be finalised after analysing stakeholders’ comments and suggestions, have a provision to extend the ‘red entry’ tag for a further period of 15 months if any subsequent incident of stubble burning is found on that land or the erring farmers fail to pay environmental compensation (fine) within the first tag period.The existing rules, framed in April 2023 and amended to increase quantum of fine in Nov 2024, have the provision for ‘red entry’ till the penalty by the erring farmer is made, but the draft of the new rules proposes land record-based compliance mechanism by introducing the continuation of the tag for 15 months and its further extension for the next 15 months in case of repeat incidents of stubble burning.Stakeholders are expected to send their comments and suggestions to the ministry within 60 days. The draft was published on Wednesday.The proposed new rules retain the existing quantum of penalty provisions whereby the farmers having an area of land of less than two acres will have to pay an environmental compensation (fine) of Rs 5,000 per incident; those having an area of land of two acres or more but less than five acres need to pay Rs 10,000 per incident; and the farmer having an area of land of more than five acres will have to pay Rs 30,000 per incident as a penalty.The fine collected under the rule will be deposited in the account of the respective State Pollution Control Board or Pollution Control Committee.The draft proposes that the collected amount will be utilised for various activities including subsidising residue management technologies such as in-situ crop residue management equipment and machinery; incentivising crop diversification programmes; and supporting development and operation of biomass utilisation and storage infrastructure among others in Delhi-NCR and adjoining areas.
Article Summary: The rules, once finalised, will be applicable in Delhi, Punjab, Haryana and National Capital Region (NCR) of Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh. Officials hinted that they may potentially disallow farmers to sell their lands and stop them from availing benefits of govt schemes.

Article Title: Maldives settles $150m India loan; final $50m tranche paid after six extensions
Article Text:

The Maldives has fully repaid a $150 million Treasury bill facility subscribed by the State Bank of India (SBI) in 2019, with the final $50 million tranche settled on September 17, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said on Friday.MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the facility had been extended six times, with the final tranche marking the completion of the repayment.“The final tranche of US dollars 50 million Treasury bills, out of a total of US dollars 150 million subscribed by the State Bank of India with the Government of Maldives, has been successfully settled on 17th September,” Jaiswal said at a media briefing.The $150 million Treasury bills were subscribed by SBI in 2019 as part of financial support to the Maldives. While the Maldivian government repaid the principal, India covered the interest costs associated with the facility.“It may also be noted that while the principal amount of the Treasury bills was paid by the Government of Maldives, the interest payment of all the US dollars 150 million Treasury bills over the past five years was borne by the Government of India,” Jaiswal said.“The total amount paid by India in interest settlement was close to US dollars 45 million,” he added.The repayment comes as the Maldives continues to manage its debt obligations and foreign exchange position. Its Ministry of Finance said the government had made arrangements to ensure that debt servicing would not disrupt imports of essential commodities, including fuel, food and medical supplies.“The Government has also put in place the necessary arrangements to ensure the continued availability of foreign currency for the import of essential goods, including fuel, food items and medical supplies,” the ministry said.“Safeguarding the uninterrupted supply of these essential goods and services remains a key priority of the Government.”India continues to provide financial support to the Maldivian financial system. Jaiswal said New Delhi had extended an Rs 30 billion currency swap facility to the Maldives, while SBI has subscribed to $350 million worth of Maldivian Treasury bonds valid until 2029 and 2030.“In addition, the State Bank of India has also subscribed to US dollars 350 million worth of Treasury bonds which are valid till 2029 and 2030.”The MEA also said the two countries continue to cooperate on development projects and supplies of essential commodities.The Maldives government, meanwhile, said it was continuing discussions with international financial institutions and bilateral partners to strengthen its foreign exchange position.
Article Summary: The Maldives has fully repaid a $150 million Treasury bill facility subscribed by the State Bank of India in 2019. While the Maldivian government repaid the principal, India covered the interest costs associated with the facility. The repayment comes as the Maldives continues to manage its debt obligations and foreign exchange position.

Article Title: CM Vijay to launch one-gram gold ring scheme for babies born in Tamil Nadu govt hospitals

Tamil Nadu govt to provide one-gram gold rings to newborns

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay will launch the one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns on September 28, the state government said. The one-gram gold rings will be provided to babies born in government hospitals under the scheme.The rings will have a unique serial number and be packed in tamper-proof packaging, the government said. As many as 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings have been procured for the first instalment of the scheme.The government said beneficiaries must be permanent residents of Tamil Nadu to be eligible for the one-gram gold ring scheme.Vijay had announced the one-gram gold ring scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme will have retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday. A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.The state has allocated around Rs 755.83 crore annually for the scheme, which will cover newborns delivered at government institutions. The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings and supply them based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee the implementation and monitoring of the scheme.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The scheme is open to Tamil Nadu residents whose children are born at government institutions. Mothers will have to submit proof of residence, with documents including ration cards, voter identity cards, Aadhaar, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates accepted.The government said the initiative was aimed at combining cultural significance with public healthcare.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay will launch the one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns on September 28. The rings will have a unique serial number and be packed in tamper-proof packaging. The scheme will have retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.

NEW DELHI: Father of one of the victims in the 2006 Nithari case questioned the death of Surendra Koli in Haridwar on Friday, alleging he was murdered and did not die by suicide."Surendra Koli has been murdered; he has not died by suicide", said Jhabbu Lal (64), whose then 15-year-old daughter was among the victims.Koli was found hanging at a rented tea stall on Friday on Sapt Sarovar Road in Haridwar. Police said the scene was examined by a forensic team, with the body's panchanama and post-mortem proceedings under way.Police said the death appeared to be a case of suicide, a claim questioned by Lal."If he had died by suicide in jail, it could be understood that he was depressed. But he took his life after being released and spending several months outside? This raises questions," he said, alleging that Koli could have been killed if he was about to disclose some important case-linked information.He also claimed that Koli was not the main culprit in the Nithari case and accused businessman Moninder Singh Pandher of being one.Koli reportedly worked as a domestic help at Pandher's Noida Sector 31 house."His owner Moninder Pandher was the main accused in the case. He should be hanged," Lal said.Lal and his wife Sunita, 61, have spent nearly 20 years seeking justice for their daughter.According to PTI, the couple hail from Uttar Pradesh’s Unnao district and had moved to Nithari about four decades ago in search of work.Lal made a living by ironing clothes for local residents.“If the government helps us, only then will we be able to continue our fight in future. We can’t fight on our own,” Lal said.The Nithari case came to light in 2006 after skeletal remains, skulls and bones were found in the backyard and drains near Pandher’s D-5 bungalow in Sector 31, Noida.The discovery brought to light the disappearance and killings of several children and young women, sparking nationwide outrage. The findings also left local residents fearful about allowing their children to go out alone.
